mainTopic: Why פיגול and נותר make hands טמא, and the minimum size for that טומאה; then a new משנה on whether the ברכה over the קרבן פסח covers the חגיגה (זבח) and vice versa
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion from the previous daf about why פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא. The גמרא shows that רב הונא and רב חסדא do not really argue about the reason. One explained the decree for פיגול, because of כהנים suspected of ruining קרבנות on purpose. The other explained it for נותר, because of lazy כהנים who might not finish eating in time. They do truly argue about the minimum size: one says a כזית, following the size of the איסור of eating, and the other says a כביצה, following the normal size for food טומאה. Then a new משנה asks whether one ברכה can cover both the קרבן פסח and the חגיגה (called זבח) eaten on the night of פסח. רבי ישמעאל says the פסח ברכה covers the זבח, but not the reverse. רבי עקיבא says each needs its own ברכה. The גמרא explains that the argument depends on the blood service: for רבי ישמעאל, זריקה (the חגיגה) is included in שפיכה (the פסח), but not the reverse. For רבי עקיבא, neither is included in the other.

steps.title: The two reasons are not a dispute: each applies to a different case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא and רב חסדא were not arguing about the reason. One gave his reason about פיגול, and the other gave his reason about נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One taught his reason about פיגול, and the other taught his reason about נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the earlier disagreement between רב הונא and רב חסדא by saying they were each talking about a different item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it looked as if the two אמוראים gave competing reasons for why פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא. Now the גמרא says each reason was given for only one of the two items, so the two reasons can both be true. The next step spells out which reason goes with which item.

keyTerms.meaning: One (of them) taught
A קרבן ruined by a wrong intention during the עבודה (e.g., planning to eat it after its time)
Leftover קרבן meat that remained past its permitted time

phrases.english: One taught (his reason) about פיגול,
phrases.notes: אַפִּיגּוּל is a short way of saying עַל פִּיגּוּל, 'regarding פיגול'.

phrases.english: and one taught (his reason) about נותר.
phrases.notes: אַנּוֹתָר is a short way of saying עַל נוֹתָר.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד תָּנֵי אַפִּיגּוּל, וְחַד תָּנֵי אַנּוֹתָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent dispute between רב הונא and רב חסדא from the previous daf about the reason for the decree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (לא פליגי, each Sage spoke about a different item)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like the two אמוראים argued about one reason covering both פיגול and נותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no argument. Each reason belongs to a different item.

steps.title: Matching each reason to its case
steps.stepSummary: The decree for פיגול is because of כהנים suspected of ruining קרבנות on purpose. The decree for נותר is because of lazy כהנים who would not finish eating on time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who taught it about פיגול: the reason is suspected כהנים. The one who taught it about נותר: the reason is lazy כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which reason goes with which item, finishing the answer from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פיגול, a כהן might spitefully ruin someone's קרבן by thinking a wrong thought. The חכמים made the פיגול meat טמא so that the כהן would suffer too, since he would then become טמא from it. With נותר, the חכמים made the leftover meat טמא so that lazy כהנים would make sure to eat the meat in time.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים suspected of wrongdoing, here spoiling a קרבן on purpose
Lazy כהנים who would not finish eating the meat in time
Because of

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול leads to טומאה because of suspicious כהנים. נותר leads to טומאה because of lazy כהנים. Both are rabbinic decrees meant to change how the כהנים behave.

phrases.english: The one who taught it about פיגול —
(says it is) because of suspected priests.
phrases.notes: Priests who might ruin a קרבן out of spite

phrases.english: The one who taught it about נותר —
(says it is) because of lazy priests.
phrases.notes: So that they make sure to eat the meat within its time

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the details of the answer given in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the details of the case split
steps.terutzMaskana: Each reason fits its own item: suspicion fits פיגול, and laziness fits נותר.

steps.title: A real dispute about the minimum size
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא do truly argue about how much meat makes something טמא. One says a כזית and the other says a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said an olive's bulk, and the other said an egg's bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second, real disagreement between the two אמוראים, about the minimum amount needed. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the reasons in steps 1 and 2, this is a true argument. The question is how much פיגול or נותר is needed to make the hands טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's bulk, the standard minimum for forbidden eating
An egg's bulk, the standard minimum for food to pass on טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two disagreements. The 'reason' disagreement was settled in steps 1 and 2. This 'size' disagreement stays a real argument.

phrases.english: One said an olive-bulk
and one said an egg-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר כְּזַיִת וְחַד אָמַר כְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first disagreement (the reason) to the second disagreement (the size).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute over whether the minimum size of פיגול or נותר that makes the hands טמא is a כזית or a כביצה.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each size
steps.stepSummary: The כזית view compares this טומאה to the איסור of eating, which starts at a כזית. The כביצה view compares it to normal food טומאה, which starts at a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says a כזית holds it is like its prohibition. The one who says a כביצה holds it is like its טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא picked his size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side copies an existing measurement. One view says this decree follows the איסור of eating פיגול and נותר, which is a כזית. The other view says that since this is about טומאה, it follows the normal rule that food passes on טומאה only at a כביצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Like its prohibition, measured by the eating איסור (a כזית)
Like its טומאה, measured by the normal size for food טומאה (a כביצה)

steps.whatToRemember: כזית follows the איסור. כביצה follows טומאה. The argument is about which existing measurement this decree should copy.

phrases.english: The one who said an olive-bulk — (holds it is) like its prohibition,
and the one who said an egg-bulk — (holds it is) like its impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for each side of the dispute in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כזית view follows the size of the איסור. The כביצה view follows the size of normal food טומאה.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי ישמעאל on the blessings for the פסח and the offering
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. According to רבי ישמעאל, the ברכה over the קרבן פסח also covers the זבח (the חגיגה), but the ברכה over the זבח does not cover the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said the ברכה for the פסח, he has covered the זבח. If he said the ברכה for the זבח, he has not covered the פסח. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks whether one ברכה over eating a קרבן can cover a second קרבן eaten at the same meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the night of the 15th of ניסן people ate both the קרבן פסח and the חגיגה of the 14th, and each has its own ברכה: 'לאכול את הפסח' and 'לאכול את הזבח'. רבי ישמעאל says the coverage works in one direction only. The פסח ברכה covers the זבח, but not the reverse. Step 7 explains why, based on how the blood of each קרבן is put on the מזבח: poured (שפיכה) for the פסח, thrown (זריקה) for the חגיגה. זריקה is included in שפיכה, but not the reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה': the start of a new משנה
He recited a ברכה
He exempted, meaning the ברכה covered the other item
Here, the חגיגה (שלמים offering) of the 14th, eaten along with the פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'זבח' does not mean any sacrifice in general. It means the specific חגיגה offering eaten together with the קרבן פסח.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one recited the blessing of the Paschal lamb —
phrases.notes: 'אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לאכול את הפסח'

phrases.english: he has exempted that of the offering (the חגיגה).
If he recited that of the offering —
he has not exempted that of the Paschal lamb,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּירַךְ בִּרְכַּת הַפֶּסַח פָּטַר אֶת שֶׁל זֶבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the טומאה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, the פסח ברכה covers the זבח, but the זבח ברכה does not cover the פסח.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: each offering needs its own blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees and says neither ברכה covers the other. Each קרבן needs its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: this one does not cover that one, and that one does not cover this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי עקיבא's opposing view: the ברכות never cover each other, in either direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל allowed coverage in one direction. רבי עקיבא allows it in neither direction. In his view the two ברכות are separate, so a person eating both קרבנות must say both ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempts, meaning covers (feminine, referring to the ברכה)
Neither this one... nor that one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: the פסח ברכה covers the זבח, but not the reverse. רבי עקיבא: neither covers the other, so you say two separate ברכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
This (blessing) does not exempt that one,
and that one does not exempt this one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא זוֹ פּוֹטֶרֶת זוֹ וְלֹא זוֹ פּוֹטֶרֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי ישמעאל in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the ברכות of the פסח and the זבח do not cover each other, so each needs its own ברכה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reason: throwing is included in pouring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that for רבי ישמעאל, זריקה is included in the bigger category of שפיכה, but שפיכה is not included in זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: When you look into it, you will find that according to רבי ישמעאל, throwing the blood (זריקה) is included in pouring the blood (שפיכה). But pouring is not included in throwing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It gives the reason for רבי ישמעאל's one-way rule from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of the פסח is poured (שפיכה), and the blood of the חגיגה is thrown (זריקה). Since זריקה fits inside the wider category of שפיכה, a ברכה on the פסח covers the חגיגה too. Since שפיכה does not fit inside זריקה, a ברכה on the חגיגה cannot cover the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
When you look into it, you will find. A phrase that opens an explanation
Throwing (sprinkling) the blood of a קרבן onto the מזבח. This is done for the חגיגה
Pouring the blood onto the base of the מזבח. This is done for the פסח
Included in, part of the category of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up which קרבן gets which action. The פסח is the one whose blood is poured (שפיכה). The חגיגה is the one whose blood is thrown (זריקה). So 'זריקה is included in שפיכה' means the פסח ברכה can cover the חגיגה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ברכה rule is not random. It comes from how the blood service of each קרבן is done.

phrases.english: GEMARA: When you look into it, you will find
phrases.notes: An opening phrase for an explanation of the משנה.

phrases.english: according to the words of Rabbi Yishmael:
throwing is included in pouring.
phrases.notes: So the פסח ברכה (pouring) covers the חגיגה (throwing).

phrases.english: But pouring is not included in throwing.
phrases.notes: So the חגיגה ברכה does not cover the פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's position in the משנה (Step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי ישמעאל, זריקה is a sub-type of שפיכה, but שפיכה is not a sub-type of זריקה. This explains the one-way coverage of the ברכה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's reason: the two are completely separate
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא, שפיכה is not included in זריקה, and זריקה is not included in שפיכה, so each קרבן needs its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, pouring is not included in throwing, and throwing is not included in pouring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation by giving the reason for רבי עקיבא's view from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא sees שפיכה and זריקה as two different acts, and neither one is part of the other. So a ברכה on one קרבן cannot cover the other, in either direction. This matches his rule that each קרבן needs its own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who argues with רבי ישמעאל in the משנה
The blessing said before doing the מצוה of the קרבן
According to the words (view) of

steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת depends on one question: is זריקה (the חגיגה) included in שפיכה (the פסח)? רבי ישמעאל says yes, but only in one direction. So the פסח ברכה covers the חגיגה. רבי עקיבא says no, in both directions. So each קרבן gets its own ברכה.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Akiva:
pouring is not included in throwing,
and throwing is not included in pouring.
phrases.notes: Neither act covers the other, so neither ברכה covers the other קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation by giving רבי עקיבא's side, in contrast to רבי ישמעאל's view in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי עקיבא, שפיכה and זריקה are fully separate. Neither includes the other, so each קרבן requires its own ברכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא depends on whether זריקה falls within the category of שפיכה.
